column2: Of building a temple for Shiva, Brahma, the Sun, Ganesha, Chandi, Lakshmi and the like, the merit is greater than making an image.
In installing images and in worship there is no end to the fruit. Clay is meritorious, wood more, brick-less wood more,
stone from brick more, and gold and the like gives more fruit. Sin done in seven births is destroyed from the very beginning.
By a temple he becomes a dweller in heaven and does not go to hell. Having lifted up a hundred families, the man leads them to Vishnu's world.
Yama said to Yama's servants regarding the builders of god's temples: "Men who have worshipped images and the like are not to be led to hell.
Those who do not build temples and the like are to be brought within range. Disperse as is just; let my command be obeyed.
Beings will not break your command anywhere. Only those who have taken refuge in the endless father of the world,
they are to be avoided by you; there is no place for them here. And those in the world who with minds on the Lord, devoted to him,
always worship Vishnu — they are to be avoided from very far. Whoever, standing, sleeping, going, rising, stumbling, staying,
chants Govinda — they are to be avoided from very far. Those who worship the god Janardana with daily and occasional rites
are not to be looked at by you; going to him, they go to his goal. Those who worship with flowers, incense, garments and very dear ornaments,
are not to be taken — men gone to Krishna's abode. Those who plaster and those devoted to sweeping
in Krishna's abode — leave them, their sons and their family. He by whom Vishnu's dwelling has been built, from that family
a hundred men are not to be seen by you with evil mind. But he who has a temple of Vishnu made of wood or stone,
or even of clay, is freed from all sins. The great fruit of one who sacrifices daily with sacrifice,
that fruit he obtains who has Vishnu's banner made. A hundred coming families and a hundred past
the builder of the Lord's abode leads to the world of Achyuta. Vishnu, made of seven worlds — whoever makes his house
carries across imperishable worlds and attains imperishable ones. As many years as the arrangement of bricks stays,
so many thousands of years the maker stays in heaven. The maker of an image reaches Vishnu's world, the installer is absorbed in Hari; the maker of the consecration of a temple-model is within range.
Agni said: Those told by Yama did not lead him who made the consecration and so on of Hari. Hayashirsha told Brahma about the installation of gods.
Kamarupa, Kalinga, Utkala, Kanchi, Kashmir, Kosala; space, wind, fire, water, earth — the five nights;
the unconscious, filled with darkness, without the Pancharatra; "I am Brahma, Vishnu, spotless" — one who knows thus is the teacher.
Even though lacking all marks, that teacher is master of the tantras. The gods are to be established facing the city, not turned away.
At Kurukshetra, Gaya and the like, and near rivers; Brahma in the middle of the city; in the east Indra's is lovely;
in the fire direction Agni's, of the Mothers, of the spirits and of Yama; in the south of Chandika and of the fathers, demons and the like;
in the southwest one should make a temple; in the west Varuna's; in the northwest of Vayu and of the Naga; in the north of Yaksha and Guha;
in the northeast of Chandisha and Mahesha, and Vishnu's everywhere. Not oppressing an earlier temple with a small shrine,
one who knows should not make one equal or larger. Leaving a boundary twice the extent of both, equal to the height,
one should build another temple; the wise should not oppress both. When the ground is purified one should take possession of the land.
Up to the boundary of the enclosure then one should offer the offering to beings: beans, turmeric powder with parched grain, curds and barley meal;
scattering barley meal with the eight-syllable mantra in the eight directions: "Whatever Rakshasas and Pishachas stay on this ground,
let them all depart; I shall make a place for Hari." Having had it plowed by a plow and torn up by cows,
by eight atoms a "trasarenu" is declared.
By eight of them a hair-tip, by eight a "likhya"; by eight lice, and eight of them a barley-middle;
by eight barleys a finger; a cubit is twenty-four fingers; with four more fingers, that hand is the "lotus-hand."
Having placed with this mantra the bricks, the best by region and order, one should then perform the garbha-placement, composed, in the middle place.
Above the pot, having placed the lord of gods and the lotus goddess, clays, flowers, minerals and jewels,

metals, the missile of the guardian of the quarter — one should worship in the germ-vessel. In a copper vessel shaped like a lotus, twelve fingers wide and four fingers high, one should worship the earth:

Lone one, lady of all beings, adorned with mountain seats,
agnipuran:41:22	surrounded by the ocean, you, goddess, take the germ. Nanda, make glad, Vasishthi, with the Vasus and with offspring;
agnipuran:41:23	Jaya, descendant of Bhrigu, bringer of victory to creatures; Purna, descendant of Angiras, make me fulfilled;
agnipuran:41:24	Bhadra, descendant of Kashyapa, make my mind auspicious. Endowed with all seeds, covered with all jewels and herbs,
agnipuran:41:25	Jaya, Surucira, Nanda, Vasishthi, delight here. Daughter of Prajapati, goddess, four-sided, greatest,
agnipuran:41:26	fortunate, brilliant, Bhadra, Kashyapi, delight in the house. Worshipped, most wonderful, adorned with scent and garlands,
agnipuran:41:27	bringer of prosperity, goddess, Bhargavi, delight in the house. In the possession of the lord of the region, lord of the town, lord of the house,
agnipuran:41:28	for the satisfaction of men and the rest, increase our cattle. So saying, one should sprinkle the pit with cow's urine.
Having done so one should place the germ; the germ-placement should be at night. One should give cows, clothes and the like to the teacher and food to others.
Having placed the germ and the bricks, one should then fill up the germ; then one should make the base-binding according to the measure of the temple.
The best base is of half the width of the temple in height; the middle is less by a quarter; the lowest is half the best.
Above the base-binding one should again perform the site-sacrifice; the maker of the foundation is sinless and rejoices in heaven.
Whoever thinks in mind "I shall build a temple," the sin in his body perishes that very day.
What then of him who has done it, by rule, in the temple? Whoever builds a shrine of the deity with eight bricks,
no one can speak the fruit and prosperity of that. By this alone the fruit may be inferred from the temple's extent.

In the middle of the village and in the east one should arrange a west-facing door; in all intermediate directions, in a village it should be west-facing; in the south, north and west it should be east-facing.
By the length of the wall one should plan the height; double the wall height one should plan the spire, the wise one.
By a quarter of the spire one should arrange the circumambulation; by a quarter of the spire in front the entrance hall.
By an eighth of the sanctum the projection of the offsets; by a third part of the circumference one should arrange the offsets there.
Or by a third of that one should make the projection of the offsets; three left ones should always be set on the three offsets.
For the spire one should drop four lines; one should drop the line across above the parrot-nose (shukanasa).
At half the spire one should make a lion there; having fixed the shukanasa one should set it in the middle joint.
On the other side likewise one should set the line; above that is the altar, thorny, with a pole.
It should not be shoulder-broken nor ugly; above, by the measure of the altar, one should plan the pot.
The door should be made twice the width, very beautiful; the thresholds and above them one should place the frame with auspicious things.
In a quarter of the door the two Chanda and Prachanda should be made; Vishvaksena and Vatsa with staves; above the crest, at the lintel, Shri,
bathed by elephants of the quarters with pots, with a lotus, well formed. The height of the enclosure should be a quarter of the temple.
The height of the gate-tower should be less than the temple by a quarter. For a god of five cubits the pedestal is one cubit.
One should make a Garuda pavilion in front, and one earth-level and other abode for an image, in the directions and above at the eight places.
In the east Varaha, in the south Narasimha, Shridhara in the water; in the north Hayagriva; in the southeast Jamadagnya;

in the southwest Rama, in the west Vamana and Vasudeva; in the northeast the temple composition should be given with the Vasus, Adityas and the like. Leaving off an eighth part and so on of the door, the piercing is not faulty.
On a stone, a white line at the top, or dark at the top, from the Simha oblation; it would sound like a bronze bell, male, a sparkle.
One with faint marks would be female; for lack of form, a eunuch. One in which a circle is seen is pregnant; reject it.
For an image one should go to the forest and perform the Vraja sacrifice. There, having dug and plastered, one should worship Hari in the pavilion.
Having given the offering, one should worship the work-tools such as the chisel; having offered, one should sprinkle the stone with rice-water and the weapon-mantra.
Having made protection with Narasimha, one should worship with the root-mantra; having offered, one should give the full oblation, then the teacher the offering to beings.
Whatever beings stay here, Yatudhanas and Guhyakas, Siddhas and others, and any others — having worshipped them, I ask forgiveness.
